content:
maria: fyi customer Brightline reporting embeddings throughput collapse — vectors/sec dropped ~4x around 03:00 UTC but tokens/sec looks stable. They see long queue depths and intermittent 429s.

jonathan: ugh. any error body from API? batching window metrics?

maria: pasted the customer error snippet: 
```
{
  "status": 429,
  "error": "queue_full",
  "detail": "enqueue failed: max_inflight_batches_exceeded"
}
```

rahul: quick telemetry: their per-route vecs/s dropped 11.9k -> 2.8k at 03:02 UTC. GPU utilization on the serving cluster stayed ~98% during the drop. tokens/sec measured by tokenizer probes stayed ~steady (±5%).

sre-jen: can you paste nvidia and pod queue snapshots? also any rollout around that time?

maria: rollout bot shows no canary at 02:50-03:10. logs from one pod: 
```
[03:02:17] WARN batching: microbatch window triggered early, batch_size=2 (expected ~16)
[03:02:17] INFO kernel-select: falling back to kernel=fp32_generic due to quantized-kernel OOM
[03:02:18] ERROR enqueue: timeout waiting for kvcache lock (client=brightline-prod-2)
```

jonathan: falling back to fp32_generic and tiny batch sizes -> explains perf. What triggered quantized-kernel OOM? model variant? memory pressure?

rahul: looked at infra metrics: host-level mem spike on rowserving node group at 02:59, pgc reclaiming pages. Also saw a sudden increase in small concurrent requests (many 1-vector requests) from that customer — their client might have changed concurrency pattern.

maria: customer insists they didn't change client. they did roll a new queuing lib internally but claim it batches locally.

ops-bot: deploybot: no infra deploys. autoscaler activity: +2 pods at 03:15 due to backlog.

jonathan: repro steps I ran locally (reliable):
```bash
# synthetic load: mix of 1-vector and 16-vector requests at 120 rps
python tools/repro/emit_embeds.py --host $ENDPOINT --concurrency 80 --mix 0.6,0.4 --vector-sizes 1,16
```
Result: when fraction of 1-vector requests >50% throughput collapses, kernels pick smaller batch windows, and FP32 fallback happens often.

maria: interesting. customer spike of 1-vector requests would increase microbatch churn and cause kv cache lock contention?

rahul: yup. KV cache lock hold times increase because more microbatches flush partial KVs. once fallback kernel triggers, per-token cost jumps and queue backs up -> 429s.

sre-jen: immediate mitigations: 1) increase max_inflight_batches limit for that route (quick rollback) 2) set temporary routing to dedicated pool with larger batch window 3) ask customer for client telemetry to confirm 1-vector spike

jonathan: also a longer-term fix: make kernel selection more tolerant to transient mem pressure and prefer quantized kernels if mem reclaim is momentary. plus better small-batch fast-path. filing engineering task.

maria: I briefed the CS lead and offered a temporary routing change; they're ok with testing. I'm going to apply a route override to direct Brightline to high-batch pool and increase inflight limit to 6.

ops-bot: route-override applied: brightline-prod -> pool-highbatch, max_inflight_batches=6 (applied by maria at 03:25 UTC)

maria: after override, customer reports vectors/sec recovered to ~10.8k and 429s dropped to zero. still watching for recurrence.

rahul: follow-ups: (a) add telemetry for per-client vector size histogram, (b) add alert when kernel fallback rate >1% of requests, (c) evaluate a fast-path for small-batch kernel to avoid FP32 fallback.

sre-jen: assigning to jonathan & rahul for the kernel/fallback investigation. tagging for postmortem if this reoccurs.

jonathan: got it — I'll open an RFC and a small benchmark harness to reproduce quantized-kernel OOMs under mixed small/large request patterns.

maria: tl;dr for support ticket: root cause likely transient client-side pattern producing many single-vector requests causing microbatch churn -> memory pressure -> kernel fallback to slower path -> throughput regression + 429s. mitigation applied and validated.

maria: closing the loop with Brightline and offering a follow-up call to review best-practice batching. :thumbsup:
